clue.text: Church council finishing early with rousing hymns lacking hard words such as faith, religion and belief

definitions.text: words such as faith, religion and belief

indicators.note: stopping before the end means the last letter of the council word is lost

parts.note: a synod is an assembly of church officials

indicators.note: rousing means stirring up, so the remaining letters of the hymns word are shaken into a new order
lacking says a letter is dropped from the word hymns

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A church synod cuts its meeting short, stirring hymns minus anything harsh, discussing faith and belief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finishing early' trims SYNOD to SYNO; 'lacking' drops H from HYMNS, and 'rousing' turns YMNS into NYMS.
explanation.definitionFit: Faith, religion and belief are near-equivalent terms, each one a word with a closely matching meaning to the others.

clue.text: Stamp bearing Queen and Queen Rat

indicators.note: bearing means carrying, so the stamp holds the queen letters

parts.note: a seal is an official stamp
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is a crossword queen
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is a crossword queen

explanation.surface: A postage stamp showing the Queen, alongside a Queen Rat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bearing' takes one Queen inside the stamp word; the second Queen is the crossword-standard ER, Elizabeth Regina. 'Rat' is a verb here, not the rodent.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to rat is to inform on someone; an informer is a grass or snitch.

clue.text: Speed past US city as young maiden

indicators.note: past says the speed letters come after the city

parts.note: NY is New York
speed is measured in mph, miles per hour

explanation.surface: A girl speeds by an American city.
explanation.definitionFit: In myth a nymph is a beautiful young female spirit, a maiden.

clue.text: Opening provided by random riots in Holland

indicators.note: in says the scrambled letters sit inside the Holland code

parts.note: NL is the international code for the Netherlands

indicators.note: random says the letters of riots are jumbled

explanation.surface: An opportunity arising from riots breaking out in the Netherlands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'random' scrambles riots, and 'in' places the result inside the country code for the Netherlands. 'Opening' looks like an opportunity but is a hole.
explanation.definitionFit: A nose has two of these openings, the holes through which we breathe.

clue.text: Leader of Exodus boarding ship to follow second prophet

indicators.note: to follow says the ship part comes after the moment word

parts.note: mo is a moment, a second

indicators.note: boarding means going aboard, so a letter goes inside the ship

parts.note: SS is steamship

indicators.note: Leader of picks out the first letter of Exodus

explanation.surface: The leader of the Exodus boards a ship following a prophet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leader of Exodus' reads as a description of the answer, but only supplies E, which 'boarding' puts on the ship; 'second' is the short word for a moment.
explanation.definitionFit: He led the Israelites out of Egypt and is revered as a prophet in several faiths — an example.

clue.text: In the thick of a smog across delta

indicators.note: across says the mist word stretches over and around the delta letter

parts.note: smog is a thick mist
D is delta in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone lost in a fog drifting over a river delta.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in the thick of something is being in its middle, surrounded by it — a synonym phrase.

clue.text: Small car problem returns for youngest family member

parts.note: the Mini is a small British car

indicators.note: returns means the problem word is read backwards

parts.note: a sum is an arithmetic problem

explanation.surface: A small car's fault resurfaces, and the youngest child gets it.
explanation.walkthrough: In British public schools the youngest of brothers was called Minimus.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for smallest, used at old British schools for the youngest of several brothers.

clue.text: Days without a drink lead to agonising stomach complaint

indicators.note: without says the letter a is taken out of the word Days
agonising begins with the letter a, so the dropped letter is led on to the end to start it

parts.note: Pepsi is a soft drink brand

explanation.surface: Days without a drink lead to an agonising stomach ache.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' takes A out of DAYS and 'lead to' puts it back at the end, where it also stands for the first letter of 'agonising'.
explanation.definitionFit: Indigestion is a digestive disorder of the stomach, the medical term naming it.

clue.text: Plots removal of men from farm vehicles

indicators.note: removal of says the men letters are taken out

parts.note: tractors are farm vehicles
OR, other ranks, means soldiers or men

explanation.surface: Taking the workers off farm vehicles on the fields.
explanation.walkthrough: OR, other ranks, is a crossword standard for men.
explanation.definitionFit: Plots of land are areas or expanses, the noun sense of tracts.

clue.text: French refusal to take in an Eastern European dictator

indicators.note: to take in means the refusal word encloses the rest

parts.note: non is French for no
an gives the letter A
a Pole is from Poland

explanation.surface: A French no to admitting an Eastern European dictator.
explanation.definitionFit: The French emperor seized and held absolute power, an example of a dictator.

clue.text: Reveals peacekeepers beginning to make requests

parts.note: UN peacekeeping forces come from the United Nations

indicators.note: beginning to picks out the opening letter of the word make

parts.note: requests as a verb means asks

explanation.surface: UN peacekeepers start making demands and expose something.
explanation.definitionFit: To reveal is to expose or show the true face of, as when taking off a disguise.

clue.text: Names muddled by one with a memory problem

indicators.note: muddled means mixed up, so the letters of Names are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone who mixes up names has a poor memory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'muddled' rearranges the five letters of Names, and the Roman one and 'a' follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Loss of memory is the medical condition named, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Wild boar drinking last of punch can't stand

indicators.note: drinking means taking in, so one piece goes inside the other
wild signals the letters of boar run riot into a new order
last of picks out the final letter of punch

explanation.surface: A wild boar slurping punch is something nobody can bear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild' turns BOAR into ABOR, and 'drinking' takes H, the last letter of punch, inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To loathe something is to be unable to bear it, a synonym.

clue.text: Most turbulent time following lies about millions

indicators.note: following puts the time letter after the rest
about says the fibs word goes round the millions letter

parts.note: stories are fibs or untruths
M is the abbreviation for million(s)

explanation.surface: A chaotic period following lies about millions — a political scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts M inside STORIES; 'following' places T after.
explanation.definitionFit: Turbulent weather is stormy, so the superlative means the wildest or roughest.

clue.text: Old Major's decoration embroidered initially onto uniform in a range of colours

indicators.note: onto places the first letter at the front of the rest
initially picks out the first letter of embroidered
in says the uniform letter sits inside the colours word

parts.note: a palette is an artist's range of colours
U is uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An old army major's insignia, embroidered on his uniform in many colours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts U inside PALETTE, giving PAULETTE.
explanation.definitionFit: An ornamental shoulder piece worn on military dress, traditionally showing an officer's rank.

clue.text: Boxer, taking drug, interrupts moans about odd events

indicators.note: interrupts says the boxer piece breaks into the other
about signals the letters of moans are turned around and rearranged

parts.note: Muhammad Ali the boxer
E is ecstasy

explanation.surface: A boxer on drugs breaks into someone's complaints about strange happenings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges moans to ANOMS; 'interrupts' puts the boxer-plus-ecstasy piece between its fourth and fifth letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Irregularities or deviations from the norm are strange occurrences, a synonym.

clue.text: Police surveillance exercises heading off to get fast food

indicators.note: heading off says the first letter is taken away

parts.note: stakeouts are police watching a place

explanation.surface: Detectives on surveillance getting fast food delivered.
explanation.definitionFit: Meals bought ready to eat away from the restaurant are quick meals, as in American usage.

clue.text: Two, tailless pigs are OK

indicators.note: Two says the shortened pig word appears twice
tailless means the final letter is cut off

parts.note: a sow is a female pig

explanation.surface: A pair of pigs with docked tails turn out fine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tailless' cuts SOW to SO, and 'Two' doubles it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something middling or passable is just about acceptable, which is what the colloquial phrase means.

clue.text: Get bigger present after small party

indicators.note: after says the present word comes behind the small letter

parts.note: the present is now
a ball is a formal dance party

explanation.surface: A gift arrives after a modest party, and the party grows.
explanation.definitionFit: Growing rapidly like a rolling ball of snow, the verb meaning to escalate.

clue.text: Grain ration endlessly redistributed

indicators.note: redistributed means shared out differently, so the letters are reordered
endlessly says the outer letters of ration are lost

explanation.surface: A grain ration shared out again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' leaves ATIO from RATION; 'redistributed' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: A grain is a tiny amount, as is a jot, the Greek letter used to mean the smallest bit.

clue.text: Minerva regularly gripped by desire to succeed

indicators.note: gripped by says those letters are held inside the desire word

parts.note: to ache for is to long for

indicators.note: regularly picks every other letter of Minerva

explanation.surface: The Roman goddess Minerva, gripped by ambition, wants to succeed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the second, fourth and sixth letters of Minerva, and 'gripped by' sets them inside the longing word before its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To accomplish or attain a goal is to succeed in it, a synonym.

clue.text: Two men consuming tail of lobster and other crustacean

indicators.note: consuming means eating, so the pair takes in the lobster letter

parts.note: king and pawn are two chessmen

indicators.note: tail of picks out the last letter of lobster

explanation.surface: Two diners eat lobster tail and another shellfish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'consuming' puts R, the last letter of lobster, inside KING and PAWN. 'Two men' looks like diners but means chess pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A large prawn is another shellfish beside the lobster, hence 'other' — an example of a crustacean.

clue.text: Fix important Eastern complaint

parts.note: to pin is to fasten or fix
key means vital or important

explanation.surface: Fixing a key complaint from the East.
explanation.definitionFit: Conjunctivitis is an infection of the eye, an example of an ailment.

clue.text: Forage crop left in shelter

indicators.note: in says the left letter goes inside the shelter word

parts.note: cover means shelter

explanation.surface: Animal fodder left under cover.
explanation.definitionFit: A leguminous plant grown to feed livestock, an example of a fodder crop.

clue.text: Hateful promises concealed by corrupt mole

indicators.note: concealed by says the promises word is hidden within the other
corrupt means warped, so the letters of mole are rearranged

parts.note: oaths are solemn promises

explanation.surface: A treacherous spy, the mole, hides broken promises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corrupt' rearranges mole as LOME, and 'concealed by' splits it after the L to hold the promises.
explanation.definitionFit: Something hateful is detestable, repellent — a synonym.

clue.text: Former faction heard to shine

indicators.note: heard says the words are spoken aloud to give a word sounding the same

parts.note: ex means former, and a cell is a faction or small group

explanation.surface: A former splinter group voices its intention to shine.
explanation.definitionFit: To shine at something is to be outstanding at it, a figurative synonym.

clue.text: Person who fails to honour commitment: not special, not at all

indicators.note: not says the special letter is left out

parts.words: Person who fails to honour commitment
parts.note: a no-show is someone who doesn't turn up as promised

explanation.surface: A judgement on an unreliable person: nothing special, nothing at all.
explanation.definitionFit: A dialect word meaning in no way or by no means whatever.

clue.text: Strong feeling about introduction of statutory speed

indicators.note: about says the hate word wraps around the letter

parts.note: hate is a strong feeling

indicators.note: introduction of picks out the first letter of statutory

explanation.surface: Strong feelings about bringing in speed limits by law.
explanation.definitionFit: Hurry or swiftness of action — a synonym for speed.

clue.text: Most proud of a home in top surroundings

indicators.note: in and surroundings together say the garment wraps around the other pieces
surroundings says the top word encloses the rest

parts.note: a vest is an upper garment, a top
in means at home

explanation.surface: A homeowner in a smart top is very proud.
explanation.definitionFit: Vain means conceited, so the superlative is the most conceited.

clue.text: Revolutionary left main London area

parts.note: Che Guevara, the Argentine revolutionary
the main is a poetic word for the sea

explanation.surface: A revolutionary left the mainland for London.
explanation.definitionFit: A fashionable district in west London, an example of a city area.

clue.text: Part of soap-opera's hero is a bit of a pig

definitions.text: is a bit of a pig

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A soap opera's leading man is a bit of a swine.
explanation.definitionFit: A slice of bacon comes from a pig, so it is literally a bit of one.

clue.text: Flower in vulgar ring

parts.note: blue jokes are risqué or vulgar
to give someone a bell is to ring them

explanation.surface: A crude ring with a flower on it.
explanation.definitionFit: A spring woodland plant with blue bell-shaped blooms, an example of a flower.
